comment.body:
Tried my best, prof. Getting some clarity, but still a lot to study and put the picture together. But these excercises are very helpful, especially with you following up later:) 

ATM: Zomma effect is negative, and steeper for high vol suppression(-40% or more suppression) otherwise flatter. So both vol up and vol down,gamma decreases, but much more for vol down, except end of week where zomma effect flips positive for high vol supression, and gamma increases. Apart from this, across time axis zomma effect is relatively flat. Conclusion: Zomma effect is present both on vol down and vol up moves and decreases gamma, starker decrease for vol suppression.

So vol up, gamma down. Vol down, gamma down even stronger.
So in both cases, vol expands (since gamma is inverse to vol.). So if call side catches a steady bid (vol down) zomma effect is going to drop gamma fast and increase vol and then zomma effects is less strong but still reducing gamma so vol increases, but less strongly than at surpression levels, so spot gets downside pressure both if it gets bid up steadily (stronger here) as well as when vol increasws, and it starts dropping.

Vomma effect is also negative, relatively flat on the vol change axis, but very steep on the time axis going to 0 vomma effect, towards end of week for suppression, and earlier for vol expansion. So for vol expansion strong vomma effect beginning of the week, and only half as strong for vol suppression, but still all vega suppressing. Conclusion: Negative vomma effect across all days, and both for vol compression and suppression, but stronger for vol expansion early in the week, and fading faster into week end for vol expansion than suppression.
So volup, vega down. Vol down, vega down but less strong. Soin both vol up and vol down, vega reduces for MM, so upward pressure on IV. Hedges more expensive. (Still unclear on spot effect here??)

Tail:
Zomma effect positive, steep profile, both across vol change and time axis(less steep here). For vol up high zomma effect, especially beginning of the week, positive zomma effect fades into week end steeply.
Almost flat 0 zomma effect for vol down into week end, more especially for high vol suppression, but for less strong vol suppression and earlier in the week steep and positive zomma effect.
Conclusion: zomma effect more focused on vol up side, but also present on voldown (and steeply).

So vol up, gamma up. Vol down, gamma up (but less strongly than vol up side).So if downside momentum accelerates, dips get bought, and vol gets surpressed, slowing downside moves, swallowing vol. But this effect decades over the week. So downside gets protected strongly early in the week and more downside risk later in the week.
Vomma effect positive, similar to zomma. Steep across vol up side, and steep across time axis but focus on vol up side. and almost flat across time, except for vol suppression at beginning of week. So vol up, vega up steeply. Vol down, small vega up effect, beginning of week. So if vol up, MM vega exposure increases steeply, so there is downward pressure on IV. (Here im still struggling how that impacts spot, or if this is all about smirk convexity and kurtosis that you mentioned during the week…so got some more studying to do. Does this just mean hedging unwinds?)

comment.body:
here's my take on charts @Alma shared - Would love inputs on if I was thinking correctly or I missed something obvious - ail Put Positioning:
There is notable long tail put positioning early in the week, suggesting the market is hedged for a volatility spike primarily in the first half of the week. This positioning fades later in the week, implying expectations for vol to calm after mid-week, particularly as this exposure rolls off following Wednesday’s VIX expiration.
ATM Gamma Regime:
ATM gamma remains negative, consistent with the broader negative gamma regime we’ve been in. However, if vol stabilizes or begins to decline, ATM gamma should increase (become less negative). Importantly, the rate of gamma improvement is steeper on vol declines than the deterioration seen on vol increases. This asymmetry gradually fades through the week as overall gamma trends less negative.
Zomma / Structural Zones:
Zomma clustering is centered around ~6416 with structure extending below 6557, driven by a concentration of OTM wing long positions. This creates a vol-up / gamma-up dynamic initially. That OTM wing concentration dissipates after Wednesday’s VIX expiration, which should naturally push the market toward less negative gamma even if vol simply stabilizes. If vol compresses, we would expect a sharp increase in ATM gamma.

Zomma tail: beginning of week steep positive zomma curve, vol up - gamma up scenario. If vol goes down, gamma is flattening, does not decrease as much as to the upside. Increased gamma begets hedge unwinds and vol selling, market well hedged to the downside setting floor at 6416.85, effect is vanishing towards the end of the week.

Zomma ATM: moderate positive slope at the beginning of the week. Vol down gamma down with acceleration for big IV decreases. Towards the end of the week starting from Wednesday the slope turns negative and is very steeply negative on Thursday with peak on Friday for downside gamma. Vol up - gamma down, less supportive flow, increased volatility end of week. 

Vomma tail: steep positive slope beginning of week, Vol up - Vega up. No decrease of Vega for vol down. Steepness decaying over week, on Friday basically flat across the whole IV range. Contributes to support in the tails early in the week. 

Vomma ATM: clearly negative slope on Monday, vol down - Vega up, slope flattening drastically over the week, only slightly negative on Friday, sensitivity/convexity going down and therefore impact is muted end of week. Early week IV priced higher making moves more erratic around cluster of 6531.73. 

Market well supported at beginning of the week, becoming increasingly vulnerable over the week. I interpret it as market hedging „weekend risk“ for the beginning of the week.

comment.body:
Woah, thanks for sharing the charts, Alma.  We now have the benefit of answering your question AFTER the post, but here's here my take:

Customer TailPut Vomma (how vega changes when vol changes)
Customers are long tail puts. Their vega sensitivity to vol increases is massive early in the week (4-8M at 3/14 with +60% IV) and decays sharply toward 3/20. Vomma shrinks as time to expiry shrinks.  If vol spikes Monday, these tail puts gain enormous vega exposure (their vol sensitivity compounds on itself). By Friday, the same vol spike produces a fraction of the vega gain. The customer's purchased convexity is a wasting asset…. most potent now, weakest at 

Customer ATM Vomma
Customers vomma is entirely negative, reaching -8M to -10M in the late-week/high-vol corner. When vol rises, customers' short ATM position bleeds accelerating vega.  They become more short vega exactly as vol is expanding, and this gets worse as the week progresses. Assuming this is an iron fly's it highlights a core risk: the body punishes more severely as time passes and vol rises. Early in the week, the wings (shown in the first image) offset this pain. By Friday, the wings have decayed and the body dominates.

Customer TailPut Zomma (how gamma changes when vol changes)
Customers' tail puts gain gamma when vol rises (+2,500-3,000 at 3/14 with +60% IV), front-loaded and decaying like vomma but at a slower decay rate. This is like a bridge between vol space and spot space: a vol spike makes customers' puts more gamma-rich, meaning their delta accelerates faster toward the tails. Early-week vol spikes give customers responsive, convex protection. By Friday, the same vol spike gives them much less additional gamma — their tail puts behave more like static delta positions and less like convex options.

Customer ATM Zomma
Customers are short the ATM presumably, so early in the week if vol drops, their short gamma exposure intensifies. Late in the week if vol rises, their short gamma exposure deepens dramatically. The crossover from positive to negative occurs approximately mid-week.  Before Wednesday, the ATM zomma environment is still partially constructive for an iron fly. After Wednesday, it turns destructive — the body's gamma risk accelerates in a vol-up scenario, and the wings (from TailPut Zomma chart) have decayed too much to compensate.
